entities.title: No sign-in: players join by link and name only
entities.summary: Kvarðinn was first written with no sign-in: anyone with the room's link typed a name, picked a team and played. The owner replaced this with invite-only play on icelander.net (invite-only); the standalone environment keeps it.
entities.context: The requester asked for a party game with "no logins": everyone in a room, some in it and some remote, joins from one shared link on their own phone. The repository's convention (AGENTS.md, "Sign-in") is that every game's Worker checks icelander.net's sign-in with vendor/icelander-auth/; this game departs from it.

options.title: No sign-in; a seat is a name and a secret token kept in the browser
options.consequences: Anyone can join from a link with nothing to set up. Anyone who learns or guesses a live room's code can join it or watch it as a big screen; the host can remove a player. Room creation is open to anyone.

options.title: icelander.net sign-in, as every other game
options.consequences: Follows the repository's convention and limits play to people with the games:play role, but every guest needs an icelander.net account before they can join, which is what the requester asked not to have.

entities.decision: No sign-in at first. Superseded on 2026-11-23 by invite-only: on icelander.net every request now needs the games:kvardinn role. Inside a room a player is still seated by addPlayer() with a name and a seat token, saved per room in localStorage, that gets the seat back after a refresh; the standalone environment (OPEN "1") still has no sign-in.
entities.rationale: The requester's "no logins" was the point of the game; the owner chose to publish it on icelander.net behind the invite-only role instead.

origin.description: The request for the game asked for "no logins": players join from a shared link with only a name.

relationships.description: The owner put the game behind icelander.net's sign-in, for invited players only.

entities.title: An authoritative Durable Object per room, not the games hub's relay
entities.summary: Each room is Kvarðinn's own Durable Object, which holds the game, applies every move with the rules and sends each device its own view, instead of relaying messages between browsers through the games hub.
entities.context: Rally, Hivestorm and Shatterbelt play online through the games hub's relay at /games/multiplayer/match/{ID}, which forwards every message to every browser in the match. In Kvarðinn the round's target is hidden from everyone but the clue-giver until the reveal; through a relay, some browser would have to hold the target and every other device would receive it in its frames.

options.title: The games hub's relay
options.consequences: One lobby and one relay for every game, but the hidden target would reach every device.

options.title: Kvarðinn's own Durable Object running the rules
options.consequences: The target leaves the server only to the clue-giver's sockets; the room survives refreshes and drops because the game is in storage. The game carries its own Durable Object class and migration, and is not in the hub's multiplayer lobby.

entities.decision: worker/room.ts is a Durable Object named after the room code. It keeps the Game in storage, applies each action with act(), and sends every socket viewFor(game, its seat), which carries the target only for the clue-giver until the reveal. Pointer drags send only the new position.
entities.rationale: The hidden target must never reach a non-clue-giver's device, and only a server that runs the rules can keep it there. test/engine.test.ts and test/e2e.mjs check it.

origin.description: Follows from the game's rules: only the clue-giver may see the target.

sources.symbol: the target reaches only the clue-giver until the reveal

relationships.description: The other games' online rooms moved to the hub; this game keeps its own, for the reason above.

entities.title: On icelander.net, for invited players only (games:kvardinn)
entities.summary: Kvarðinn is published at icelander.net/games/fresh/kvardinn, and every request there (the page, room creation and the room WebSockets) needs icelander.net's sign-in and the invite-only role games:kvardinn, granted at icelander.net/private/admin.
entities.context: The game was written with no sign-in (no-sign-in), and merging deploys it to icelander.net, where every other game is behind the sign-in. The owner was asked whether to publish it openly, behind the sign-in, or only on a separate workers.dev account.

options.title: Publish publicly at icelander.net/games/fresh/kvardinn, no sign-in
options.consequences: Guests join with nothing to set up; icelander.net hosts a page open to anyone, with no rate limit on room creation.

options.title: Behind icelander.net's sign-in, for holders of an invite-only role
options.consequences: Like Pinochle, Iron Haze and the other invite-only games: only invited players can open the page, create rooms or join them. Every player, the big screen included, needs an icelander.net account with games:kvardinn.

options.title: Host it only on a separate workers.dev account
options.consequences: Keeps it off icelander.net; the default route would have to go before merging.

entities.decision: Invite-only on icelander.net. worker/handler.ts checks AUTH.requireRole(games:kvardinn) for every request: a visitor who isn't signed in is sent to sign in, a signed-in player without the role gets a page saying so, and the API and WebSockets answer 401 or 403. The standalone environment sets OPEN "1" and keeps the game open there.
entities.rationale: The owner's choice: "merge it and publish to icelander.net, as a game under games/, invite only".

origin.description: The owner answered the open question publish-without-sign-in: publish on icelander.net, invite only.
